questions.text: Describe the stages in a computer-controlled greenhouse temperature system.

answer.text: A sensor measures temperature and an ADC converts the signal
The computer compares the reading with the set point
It sends a signal to an actuator controlling a heater or ventilation

questions.text: A heater turns on below 18 °C and off above 20 °C. Explain why two thresholds can be useful.

answer.text: It reduces frequent switching when readings fluctuate around a single threshold

questions.text: Give pseudocode to repeatedly read Temperature and turn a heater ON when it is below 18, otherwise OFF.

answer.text: A loop repeatedly reads the sensor value
IF Temperature < 18 THEN heater ON ELSE heater OFF
Control also changes the system using actuators based on the readings

questions.text: Explain why an ADC is required for an analogue temperature sensor.

answer.text: The sensor produces a continuous analogue signal
The ADC converts sampled values into digital form for processing

questions.text: Give two precautions against sensor failure in a safety-critical system.

answer.text: Raise an alarm and move to a safe state if readings fail
